chapter: Dave Bartholomew band and early recording
title: First recordings with Bartholomew, Smiley Lewis and Fats Domino
summary: He recalls his first recordings, a split Fats Domino session with Jewel King where he played the solo, and learning the disc-recording process.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now this is about the time you started to record, isn't it?
I started first recording with Dave Bartholomew's band.
What year do you join Dave? I mean, what was, do you remember?
I sure don't.
Could have been, yeah.
Sometime in there.
Yeah.
I feel like I'm going to be better with dates than you. So, yeah, so you remember first recordings with Dave? I mean, with the first...
I couldn't swear to it, but I imagine it might have been Smiley Lewis or somebody like that.
Mm-hmm. Or the Fats Domino.
I think that might have...
Fat Man, Fat Man, Fat Stomino.

Well, I think that might have been after we had done some things with Smiley Lewis. Maybe I'm wrong. I don't know. But that first recording with Fats Domino was a split session. Fats Domino had a split session with a lady by the name of Jill King. Mm-hmm. She had the hit record called Three Times Seven.
Equals, yeah, equals 21.

Yeah, and I played solo on that, even though I've had people that call me from out of town in different places and say they didn't have me listed as being on that session. And I actually played the solo.
Oh, so you're not... I mean, I think I've seen discographies where you're... I think you're listed on...
Well, some other people say whoever the artist did, they got the wrong information because I played the solo.
So you were on that whole... You were on both... All four tracks in that session. What was the recording experience when you first started recording?
Well, it was on... It wasn't a tape machine. It was a...
Right.
Vast tape.
Yeah, those discs, yeah.
Disc, yeah. Yeah. And that was my first experience of, you know, recording.
Mm-hmm. And what was... How did you... How did you adapt? Was there a certain amount of adaptation to all the machinery? I mean, do you...
Not really. The only thing you were uptight about is that you didn't want to make a mistake.
Mm-hmm.
You know?
Oh, okay.
If there was a mistake, you hope it wouldn't be you because they have to break that and start all over again. All over again. You know, and... You tried to play what was called for you to play.
